title: Iman Gadzhi: The three dark sides of running an agency and how to handle them
summary: Iman covers the emotional rollercoaster, constant client churn, and the fact that you can't hide from people when running an agency. He argues for three-month minimums, treating retention as the biggest profit lever, and doing sales yourself, drawing on four years of agency experience.

principles.text: Sign every client on a three-month minimum so you have time to get results before they panic.
principles.quote: every single person watching this should be signing clients on a three-month minimum like that should just be a a given

principles.text: Retention is the biggest lever in an agency; it is easier to keep a client than to sign a new one.
principles.quote: it is much easier to keep a client than it is to sign a new one

principles.text: Raising average retention from about 7 to 10-11 months lifts profit around 50% with zero new clients.
principles.quote: i will literally make 50 more profit so hypothetically as an example i would go from 400 000 pounds a year from the agency to 600 000 pounds by signing no extra clients

principles.text: Accept churn as part of the model, since even clients getting great results can leave. Fight it with better results and incentives for longer contracts.
principles.quote: you could be getting clients incredible results and they'll still leave you right and it just comes with it it comes with having an agency

principles.text: Don't outsource sales. Do the call math; a couple of calls a day is a small price for driving revenue yourself.
principles.quote: you can outsource everything as an agency owner except for sales

principles.text: Treat the emotional swings as seasons: stop labeling things good or bad and remember this too shall pass.
principles.quote: it's really important to disassociate from or disassociate and stop labeling things as this is good this is bad it's all part of the process
